mn4:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn4:2.1: Then Jānussoṇi of the divine caste went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him,
mn4:2.2: and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said:
mn4:2.3: ‘Master Gotama, when clansmen have gone forth from the home life into homelessness out of faith in Master Gotama, do they have Master Gotama for their leader, their helper and their guide?
mn4:2.4: And do these people follow the implications of Master Gotama’s view?’
mn4:2.5: ‘That is so, divine, that is so.
mn4:2.6: When clansmen have gone forth from the home life into homelessness out of faith in me, they have me for their leader, their helper and their guide.
mn4:2.7: And these people do follow the implications of my view.’
mn4:2.8: ‘But Master Gotama, remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest are hard to endure, seclusion is hard to achieve and it is hard to enjoy isolation.
mn4:2.9: One would think the jungles must rob a bhikkhu of his mind, if he has no concentration.’
mn4:2.10: ‘That is so, divine, that is so.
mn4:2.11: Remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest are hard to endure, seclusion is hard to achieve and it is hard to enjoy isolation.
mn4:2.12: One would think the jungles must rob a bhikkhu of his mind, if he has no concentration.’
mn4:3.1: ‘Before my enlightenment, while I was still only an unenlightened Bodhisatta, I too (considered) thus:
mn4:3.2: “Remote jungle-thicket resting places are hard to endure …
mn4:3.3: the jungles must rob a bhikkhu of his mind, if he has no concentration.”
mn4:4.2: “Whenever monks or divines resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest unpurified in bodily conduct, then owing to the defect in their unpurified bodily conduct these worthy monks and divines evoke unprofitable fear and dread.
mn4:4.3: But I do not resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest unpurified in bodily conduct.
mn4:4.4: I am purified in bodily conduct.
mn4:4.5: I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places, as it were, one of the Noble Ones, with bodily conduct purified.”
mn4:4.6: Seeing in myself this purity of bodily conduct, I found great solace dwelling in the forest.
mn4:5.2: “Whenever monks or divines … unpurified in verbal conduct … evoke unprofitable fear and dread. But I … am purified in verbal conduct …” I found great solace dwelling in the forest.
mn4:5.3: ‘I (considered) thus: “Whenever monks or divines … unpurified in mental conduct … evoke great fear and dread. I am purified in mental conduct …”
mn4:8.2: “… covetous and keenly affected by lust for sensual desires …
mn4:9.4: I have a mind of loving-kindness …”
mn4:10.4: I am without lethargy and drowsiness …”
mn4:13.2: ‘ “… given to self-praise and disparagement of others …
mn4:13.4: I am not given to self-praise and disparagement of others …”
mn4:14.4: I am not subject to alarm and terror …”
mn4:15.2: “… desirous of gain, honour and renown …
mn4:19.2: “Whenever monks or divines resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest devoid of understanding and drivelling, then owing to the defect of their being devoid of understanding and drivelling, these worthy monks and divines evoke unprofitable fear and dread.
mn4:19.3: But I do not resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest devoid of understanding and drivelling.
mn4:19.5: I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest, as it were, one of the Noble ones perfect in understanding.”
mn4:19.6: Seeing in myself this perfection of understanding, I found great solace in dwelling in the forest.
mn4:20.2: “There are the specially holy nights of the (half-moon of the) Fourteenth, the (half-moon of the) Fifteenth, and the Quarter-moon of the Eighth.
mn4:20.4: Now what if I dwell on such nights as these in such awe-inspiring, horrifying abodes such as orchard shrines, woodland shrines, and tree shrines. Perhaps I too might encounter that fear and dread?”
mn4:20.5: ‘And later, on such specially holy nights as the (half-moon of the) Fourteenth, the (half-moon of the) Fifteenth, and the quarter-moon of the Eighth,
mn4:20.7: I dwelt in such awe-inspiring, horrifying abodes such as orchard shrines, woodland shrines and tree shrines.
mn4:20.8: And while I dwelt there, a wild animal would come up to me, or a peacock would knock off a branch, or the wind would rustle the leaves.
mn4:20.10: “What now if this is the fear and dread coming?”
mn4:20.12: “Why do I dwell always expecting fear and dread?
mn4:20.13: What if I subdue that fear and dread while keeping the posture that I am in when it finds me?’
mn4:20.14: ‘While I walked, the fear and dread came upon me.
mn4:20.15: I neither stood nor sat nor lay down till I had subdued that fear and dread.
mn4:20.16: While I stood, the fear and dread came upon me.
mn4:20.17: I neither walked nor sat nor lay down till I had subdued that fear and dread.
mn4:20.18: While I sat, the fear and dread came upon me.
mn4:20.19: I neither walked nor stood nor lay down till I had subdued that fear and dread.
mn4:20.20: While I lay down, the fear and dread came upon me.
mn4:20.21: I neither walked nor stood nor sat till I had subdued that fear and dread.
mn4:21.1: There are monks and divines who perceive day when it is night and perceive night when it is day.
mn4:21.2: I say that on their part that is a deluded man’s abiding.
mn4:21.3: Now I perceive night when it is night and perceive day when it is day.
mn4:21.4: Rightly speaking, were it to be said of someone:
mn4:21.5: “A being not subject to delusion has appeared in the world for the welfare and happiness of many, out of pity for the world, for the benefit, welfare and happiness of gods and men”,
mn4:21.6: it is of me indeed that rightly speaking it should be said thus.
mn4:22-26.1: Tireless energy was aroused in me and unforgetting mindfulness established, my body was tranquil and untroubled, my mind was concentrated and unified.
mn4:22-26.2: Quite secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unprofitable dhammas, I entered upon and abode in the first jhāna which is accompanied by initial and sustained application with happiness and (bodily) pleasure born of seclusion.
mn4:22-26.3: With the stilling of initial and sustained application, I entered upon and abode in the second jhāna, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind, without initial application and without sustained application, with happiness and pleasure born of concentration.
mn4:22-26.4: With the fading as well of happiness I abode in equanimity, mindful and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body, I entered upon and abode in the third jhāna, on which account Noble Ones announce: “He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.”
mn4:22-26.5: With the abandoning of (bodily) pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of (mental) joy and grief, I entered upon and abode in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
mn4:27.1: When the concentrated mind was thus quite purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, I directed, I inclined the mind to knowledge of the recollection of past life. I recollected my manifold past life.
mn4:27.2: that is to say, one birth, two births … five births, ten births … fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of (world) contraction, many aeons of (world) expansion, many aeons of (world) contraction and expansion: “There I was so named, of such a race, with such (qualities of) appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term; and passing away from there, I appeared elsewhere; and there too I was so-named, of such a race, with such (qualities of) appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term; and passing away from there I appeared here. Thus with details and particulars I recollected my manifold past life.
mn4:28.1: This was the first True Knowledge attained by me in the first watch of the night.
mn4:28.2: Ignorance was banished and true Knowledge arose; darkness was banished and light arose, as (happens) in one who abides diligent, ardent and self-controlled.
mn4:29.1: When the concentrated mind was thus quite purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady and attained to imperturbability, I directed, I inclined the mind to knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings.
mn4:29.2: With the heavenly eyesight which is purified and surpasses the human, I saw beings passing away and reappearing inferior and superior, fair and ugly, well-behaved and ill-behaved; I understood how beings pass on according to their kammas, thus: “These worthy beings who are ill-conducted in body, speech and mind, revilers of Noble Ones, wrong in their views, giving effect to wrong view in their kammas (actions), have, on the dissolution of the body, after death, appeared in a state of deprivation, in a bad destination in perdition, even in hell; but these worthy beings, who are well-conducted in body, speech and mind, not revilers of Noble Ones, right in their views, giving effect to right view in their kammas (actions), have, on the dissolution of the body, after death, appeared in a good destination, even in the heavenly world”, thus with heavenly eyesight which is purified and surpasses the human, I saw beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, well-behaved and ill-behaved; I understood how beings pass on according to their kammas.
mn4:30.1: This was the second True Knowledge attained by me in the second watch of the night.
mn4:30.2: Ignorance was banished and True Knowledge arose; darkness was banished and light arose as (happens) in one who abides diligent ardent and self-controlled.
mn4:31.1: When the concentrated mind was thus purified and bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, and become malleable, wieldy, steady and attained to unperturbability, I directed, I inclined the mind to knowledge of exhaustion of taints.
mn4:31.2: I had direct knowledge thus: “This is suffering”; I had direct knowledge thus: “This is the origin of suffering”; I had direct knowledge thus: “This is the cessation of suffering”; I had direct knowledge thus: “The is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.”
mn4:31.3: I had direct knowledge thus: “These are taints”; I had direct knowledge thus: “This is the origin of taints”; I had direct knowledge thus: “This is the cessation of taints”; I had direct knowledge thus: “This is the way leading to the cessation of taints.”
mn4:32.1: When I knew and saw thus, the mind was liberated from the taints of sensual desire, from the taints of being and from the taints of ignorance.
mn4:32.2: When liberated there came the knowledge: “It is liberated”.
mn4:32.3: I had direct knowledge thus: “Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived out, what can be done is done, there is no more of this in the beyond.”
mn4:33.1: ‘This was the third True Knowledge attained by me in the third watch of the night.
mn4:33.2: Ignorance was banished and True Knowledge arose; darkness was banished and light arose as (happens) in one who abides diligent, ardent and self-controlled.
mn4:34.1: ‘Now, divine, it might be that you (think) thus:
mn4:34.2: “Perhaps the monk Gotama is not free from lust, hate and delusion even today, which is why he still resorts to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest.”
mn4:34.3: But you should not think thus.
mn4:34.4: It is because I see two benefits that I still resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest:
mn4:34.5: I see a pleasant abiding for myself here and now, and I have pity on the future generations.’
mn4:35.1: ‘Indeed it is because Master Gotama is an Arahant and Fully Enlightened that he has pity on future generations.
mn4:35.3: The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama, as though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, holding up a lamp in the darkness for those with eyesight to see forms.
mn4:35.4: ‘I go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma and to the Sangha.
mn4:35.5: From today let Master Gotama remember me as a follower who has gone to him for refuge for life.’
